entities.summary: Niagara Falls spans the Canada–US border, with the Horseshoe, American and Bridal Veil waterfalls seen from several viewpoints.
entities.description: Niagara Falls is the waterfall complex on the Canada–US border, including Horseshoe, American and Bridal Veil Falls. Upper viewpoints, gorge views and separately ticketed close-up attractions offer different ways to appreciate the volume and force of the water. The waterfalls themselves need no single booking. Visiting both countries requires border documents and time for crossing.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The scale and powerful flow of Niagara Falls reward seeing the water from several angles, with major viewpoints available on both national sides.

entities.summary: Toronto’s CN Tower offers city and Lake Ontario views from observation levels 346 metres above the ground, with glass-floor sections.
entities.description: The CN Tower in Toronto lifts visitors to observation levels with broad views of the city and Lake Ontario. The 346-metre height and glass-floor sections make the scale tangible. Clear visibility is central to the reward, so consider the forecast before booking timed entry. EdgeWalk, the outdoor height experience, is a separate optional purchase.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The CN Tower’s height gives Toronto and Lake Ontario a striking new scale on a clear day; the observation visit does not require buying EdgeWalk.

names.canonical: Niagara Parks Power Station + The Tunnel

entities.summary: Niagara Parks Power Station in Ontario combines preserved generating machinery with a 600-metre tunnel ending at a river-level view below the falls.
entities.description: At Niagara Parks Power Station in Niagara Falls, Ontario, visitors explore a restored 1905 hydroelectric station before descending about 55 metres by lift. A 600-metre former water-outflow tunnel then leads to a river-level opening in the gorge below the falls. The tunnel is included in the station visit, rather than booked separately. It stays around 15°C, so bring a layer.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Niagara Parks Power Station in Ontario links huge historic machinery with a long underground walk and an unusual river-level view below Niagara Falls.

names.canonical: Saint Joseph's Oratory of Mount Royal

entities.summary: Saint Joseph’s Oratory is a large Catholic shrine on Montréal’s Mount Royal, with churches, devotional spaces and terraces overlooking the city.
entities.description: Saint Joseph’s Oratory on Mount Royal in Montréal is a multilevel shrine where visitors explore the crypt church, basilica and devotional spaces, then look out from the terraces. The visit combines monumental architecture with the pilgrimage history of Brother André. English is practical, and much is visual. The hillside has steep grades, though step-free access is available.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Saint Joseph’s Oratory in Montréal brings together monumental church interiors, pilgrimage history and elevated city views in a single hillside visit.

entities.summary: Allan Gardens Conservatory is a free greenhouse complex in central Toronto, with tropical plants, orchids, cacti and seasonal displays.
entities.description: Allan Gardens Conservatory in central Toronto leads visitors through five greenhouse zones of palms, tropical foliage, orchids, succulents and cacti. The historic glasshouses offer a compact plant-filled escape with year-round warmth, especially useful in poor weather. Admission is free and walk-in; access is partly step-free.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Allan Gardens Conservatory in Toronto combines well-kept plants and warm historic glasshouses in a compact visit with free admission.

entities.summary: Big River Baking Company in Bracebridge, Ontario, is a small bakery worth choosing for sourdough bread, croissants and other pastries.
entities.description: Big River Baking Company is a small artisan bakery on Taylor Road in Bracebridge, Ontario. Sourdough loaves and layered pastries such as croissants are the main reasons to stop. It makes a useful bread or pastry purchase when exploring Bracebridge or Muskoka. Visit earlier for a better selection, as popular items can sell out.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Big River Baking Company in Bracebridge gives bread and pastry lovers a clear local choice, with sourdough and croissants as its strongest draws.

entities.summary: Major’s Hill Park in central Ottawa offers short paths, lawns and views of Parliament, the Rideau Canal locks and the river.
entities.description: Major’s Hill Park is a small public park in central Ottawa, well placed for views of Parliament, the Rideau Canal locks and the river. Short paths, mature trees and lawns offer room to pause between downtown sights. Access is free and unbooked, with light walking and some step-free routes.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Major’s Hill Park in Ottawa is an easy stop for landmark and river views, with free access and green space between downtown attractions.
